message: A storm is coming from the west. Bring the boats in.

parts.name: an arrow pointing east, away from the west
a sun with a line through it

keys.text: Paint on every tower: an arrow shows where danger comes FROM.
keys.line: Lark paints a small arrow and a storm cloud at its tail on every tower wall. 'Now the arrow says where it comes from. Everyone learns it once.'

keys.text: Paint on every tower: a hand on a rope means BRING THE BOATS IN.
keys.line: Mina paints a large, bold hand and rope beside the tower doors. 'Big enough that no one leaves it out, and everyone knows what it asks.'

keys.text: Paint on every tower: lightning means a storm, so bring the boats in.
keys.line: Lark paints a lightning bolt over a boat pulled up on the shore. 'One sign, two meanings. Quick to copy. Let us hope nobody needs the second meaning without the first.'

trust.text: The drawing. Bold, simple marks got through.
trust.reply: Lark nods. 'Bold marks survive copying. But your bold arrow went the wrong way the first time. Bold is not the same as clear.'

trust.text: The key on the tower walls. We agreed what the marks mean.
trust.reply: Mina smiles. 'A picture is not a language until people agree on it. Every reader of a copy leans on an agreement they cannot see.'

trust.text: Both. The marks carried it, but only because we agreed what they meant.
trust.reply: Lark and Mina look at each other. 'That is the job of this whole city,' says Lark. 'Copies carry marks. People carry the meaning.'
